newsitem.title: CHINA: Sanonda first-half net up in slow market.
newsitem.headline: Sanonda first-half net up in slow market.

text.p: China's Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd racked up strong gains for the first half of 1997, although a weak market and rising costs narrowed profits, the company said on Tuesday.

The leading pesticide maker posted unaudited net profits of 61.20 million yuan for the first half of 1997, up 44 percent from 42.56 million in the year-ago period, the company said in a report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
It did not specify whether the figures reflected international or Chinese accounting standards.

"From the second half of 1996 to the first half of 1997... the international and domestic chemical markets were relatively sluggish," said Sanonda, which listed 115 million hard currency B shares last May.
In the first six months of 1997, turnover edged up to 470.66 million yuan from the year-ago level of 463.24 million yuan.
"At the same time coal, electricity and other energy prices have gone up, affecting costs," the report said.
It did not give a business forecast for the second half, and company officials declined comment.
Earnings per share reached 0.206 yuan in the first six months while net assets per share were 3.21 yuan. Per share figures for 1996 were not immediately available.
By the end of June, Sanonda had 297 million shares, made up of 90 million institutional shares, 92 million A shares and 115 million B shares.
